subject.title: File Browser: Remove ALLOWED_FILE_NAMES whitelist, add scope levels

question: Should Mission Control expose workspace-wide writes and/or host-system file browsing, and what permission boundary should replace the current bootstrap-file allowlist?
rationale: The remaining request changes which files operator clients can read or mutate and includes host paths outside agent workspace roots, so code inspection cannot safely choose the product/security boundary.

options.title: Workspace API First
options.body: Keep system browsing out of scope and settle the workspace-scoped read/write contract, permissions, tests, and UI through the canonical workspace-management thread.

options.title: Read-Only Workspace Only
options.body: Treat the current `agents.workspace.list/get` surface as the approved boundary and leave arbitrary workspace writes out until stronger demand or proof appears.

options.title: Separate System Browser Design
options.body: Open a dedicated security-reviewed design for host filesystem browsing with explicit operator opt-in, auditing, read/write limits, and recovery UX.

recommendation.title: Workspace API First
recommendation.body: Keep system browsing out of scope and settle the workspace-scoped read/write contract, permissions, tests, and UI through the canonical workspace-management thread.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the recently merged read-only workspace browser slice and are the strongest current owner signal for this security-sensitive gateway/mobile boundary.
